resources.string: Smarter greenhouse decisions, from sensing to harvest
GreenHands brings accurate sensor placement, AR heat-distribution visualization, crop health and harvest prediction, and recommended actions into one intelligent greenhouse workspace.

Decision Making is designed to provide recommended decisions and practical actions based on greenhouse and crop conditions. This component is coming soon and is not available in this build.

GreenHands is an AR–IoT Smart Greenhouse Platform. Heat Distribution is one of four components, alongside Sensor Placement, Harvesting and Decision Making.

The dashboard shows Preview Mode sample values and the four platform components. Heat Distribution opens crop configuration. Sensor Placement opens greenhouse scan and placement. Harvesting and Decision Making open Coming Soon pages.

After you open Heat Distribution, use Crops to configure crop, growth stage and Day/Night climate targets. Automatic calculation derives equipment thresholds. Save & Continue stores both periods before moving on. Research sources stay under the Sources tab.
Preview Mode uses labelled sample values. It does not read hardware or control equipment.
This build does not control fans, foggers or any physical equipment. Treat every reading as a sample until a live greenhouse is connected.

GreenHands is an AR–IoT Smart Greenhouse Platform designed to help growers monitor greenhouse conditions, optimize sensor placement, visualize heat distribution, assess crop health, predict harvesting time, and receive recommended actions. It brings greenhouse information, augmented-reality visualization, crop analysis and decision support into one mobile workspace.
Research prototype. Live AR, IoT hardware and greenhouse validation are not claimed in this build.
Heat Distribution suggested values are drawn from published crop-climate sources. Full references, classifications and limitations are listed under Heat Distribution → Sources.
Names, emails, optional profile photos and configuration figures stay in this session and on-device storage. The app never requests a Google account.
Live greenhouse readings are not connected. Dashboard values are Preview Mode sample values and are not live sensor readings.
Camera permission will only be requested when AR is added. Profile photos use the system Photo Picker and do not require broad storage access.
This build does not upload personal or sensor data to Firebase, a backend or any other service.

Enter the size of your real greenhouse in meters. The app builds a virtual greenhouse grid from those dimensions—this is not AR or a camera scan yet.

On a device, a later AR session will capture the greenhouse volume. In this build, Start Scan runs a deterministic simulated progress sequence so the workflow can be tested on an emulator.
Tap an empty cell to place a temperature sensor. Tap a sensor to select it, then tap another empty cell to move it.
Grid cells are greenhouse coordinates, not screen pixels. Each cell is a 48 dp touch target and the grid can scroll sideways on a phone.
Tap an empty greenhouse cell to place the next temperature sensor.
All sensor types use the same coverage radius in this build.
Same-type overlap: see Coverage by Sensor Type
Same-type overlap is listed under Coverage by Sensor Type.
Move: tap another empty cell. Occupied cells select that sensor instead.
Ready to place: %1$s. Tap an empty greenhouse cell.
Choose the sensor type first. The sensor is created only after you tap an empty greenhouse cell.
Review how active sensors cover the greenhouse grid. Coverage is calculated from the sensors you placed.
Coverage is calculated independently per sensor type. Different types covering the same cell are not overlap. Inactive sensors do not contribute.
All shows monitoring coverage: green if any sensor type reaches the cell. Yellow overlap appears only when a specific type is selected.
Yellow means two or more active sensors of this type cover the cell.
Each sensor type is calculated independently. Overlap means two or more active sensors of the same type.
No active sensors of this type — all cells are blind spots.

Coverage is independent per sensor type. Same-type overlap is yellow only when two or more active sensors of that type reach a cell. Different types covering the same cell are not overlap. Monitoring coverage means any sensor type reaches the cell.
Recommend additional sensor positions that improve same-type coverage. Existing sensors are not moved.
Optimization is simulated. Recommendations are not added until you apply them. Only the selected sensor type is optimized.
The system evaluates +1 to +4 additional sensors and recommends the smallest practical count for best coverage.
+%1$d → %2$d sensors · cov %3$s%% · blind %4$s%% · overlap %5$d · gain +%6$s%% · marginal +%7$s%%
Previewing an alternative sensor count (not the system recommendation).
Recommended: fewest additional sensors that reach the best evaluated coverage, then fewest blind spots.
No improving sensor positions found for the evaluated counts. Current placement is unchanged.
Fewer additional sensors = lower deployment requirement (no monetary cost model).
Shows same-type coverage for the selected type. Teal P markers are recommendations, not real sensors yet.
